bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in md_is_link_title OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=514122612 Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: md_is_link_title md_analyze_inlines md_process_normal_block_contents
bug_description.normalized: The saved testcase drives md4c's inline-link parser with attacker-controlled markdown in which a resolved `]` is immediately followed by `(`. `md_resolve_links()` therefore calls `md_is_inline_link_spec()`, which parses the link destination and then always probes for an optional title by calling `md_is_link_title()` with the current `off`. On the witnessed path, destination parsing leaves `off` already at the end of the only remaining line. `md_is_link_title()` skips no whitespace, does not reject `off == lines[line_index].end`, and immediately evaluates `CH(off)` in `switch(CH(off))`, reading one byte past the markdown buffer and triggering the saved heap-buffer-overflow read at `src/md4c.c:2125`.

source.description: The inline-link parser consumes attacker-controlled destination bytes and updates `off` to the byte immediately after the destination. This is the vulnerability-relevant source state that is later passed to the optional-title probe.
source.value_from: The saved 277-byte testcase first reaches inline-link parsing through the earlier `md_resolve_links()` `](` admission gate. Inside `md_is_inline_link_spec()`, `md_is_link_destination()` derives the `off` value from those attacker-controlled markdown bytes; on the witnessed path the updated `off` lands at the end of the remaining line before `md_is_link_title()` is called.

sink.description: Sink. `md_is_link_title()` dereferences the attacker-derived offset with `CH(off)` even when `off` already equals the end of the remaining markdown line, producing the saved one-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at the AddressSanitizer crash location.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After the optional whitespace pre-scan, the function assumes a title opener is present and dereferences `CH(off)` without first checking that `off` is still strictly inside the input buffer. When the caller passes an exhausted offset at line end, this missing bound check creates the overread condition consumed at the same statement.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call parses attacker-controlled bytes inside the candidate inline-link spec and updates `off` to the first byte after the destination. On the crashing input, that updated `off` lands exactly at the end of the only remaining line before the optional title probe.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific gate for the crashing path. The markdown must place `(` immediately after a resolved `]` so the parser admits the bytes after `]` to inline-link-spec parsing instead of treating the bracketed text as ordinary text or another link form.

fine_trace.note: A resolved closing `]` is immediately followed by attacker-controlled `(`, so md4c admits this bracketed construct to inline-link parsing.
The parser forwards the attacker-controlled offset of that opening parenthesis into `md_is_inline_link_spec()`, preserving the exact location where inline-link parsing starts.

`md_is_link_destination()` consumes attacker-controlled destination bytes inside the same `( ... )` spec and advances `off` to the byte immediately after the destination; on the witnessed path that new `off` is already the remaining line end.

fine_trace.code: if(md_is_link_title(ctx, lines + line_index, n_lines - line_index, off,
fine_trace.note: Even though destination parsing has already exhausted the remaining line, the function still calls `md_is_link_title()` to probe for an optional title and passes that end-of-line `off` onward.

Sink and root cause. The whitespace pre-scan left `off` unchanged at the remaining line end, but `md_is_link_title()` does not verify that a title opener byte exists before executing `CH(off)`. Reading that byte oversteps the markdown buffer and matches the saved ASan crash at `md_is_link_title():2125`.

format.name: libFuzzer testcase for fuzz-mdhtml
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact saved 277-byte `fuzz-mdhtml` testcase. Its first eight bytes are consumed by the harness as parser and renderer flags, and the remaining markdown bytes include a resolved `]` immediately followed by `(` that reaches inline-link parsing. The available artifacts prove this exact testcase drives `md_is_inline_link_spec()` to call `md_is_link_title()` with `off` already at the remaining line end; they do not prove a broader input class or that admonitions were enabled.
